rv.q: Even if occasionally the mood seems closer to Charley’s Aunt than Oscar Wilde , this is a thoroughly enjoyable production and, at its centre, lies a superb performance by Suchet that reminds us that even Lady Bracknell contains a certain impishness beneath her elegantly frocked hauteur.
But Suchet fans won't be disappointed.
From beginning to end, this production of Wilde's masterpiece displays an earnest frivolity.

cn.t: Critics praise this faithful revival for David Suchet's magnificent, scene-stealing turn as Lady Bracknell, played with impish humor and imperious command that dominates Adrian Noble's smart production.
